uses.issue: Whether post-9 June 1952 subletting, assignment or other parting with possession without written landlord consent is a section 14(1)(b) eviction ground.
uses.law_quote: sub-let, assigned or otherwise parted with the possession of the whole or any part of the premises without obtaining the consent in writing of the landlord
uses.reason: This is the supplied Delhi statutory ground governing the fixed question. It directly identifies the prohibited dispositions, the relevant date threshold and written-consent requirement; the record contains disputed allegations of subletting/parting and an asserted earlier landlord permission.
uses.standalone_value: Supplies the governing statutory elements, but alone does not determine whether the respondent actually sub-let, assigned or parted with possession or whether qualifying written consent existed.
uses.incremental_value: Provides the controlling framework against which the corporate-occupation evidence, testamentary-transfer argument and consent assertions must be assessed.
uses.limits: Current reproduction is not an authenticated historical consolidation and supplies no target-case judicial interpretation.

uses.issue: Whether the General Radio authority concerns a statutory transfer/subletting regime sufficiently similar to illuminate its later application.
uses.law_quote: without the written consent of the landlord
uses.reason: This unit states the Andhra Pradesh provision applied in General Radio. It provides context for that authority's treatment of amalgamation and written consent, but it is expressly not Delhi law and does not itself govern the supplied section 14(1)(b) dispute.
uses.standalone_value: Shows the statutory setting of General Radio, including a written-consent restriction on transfer or subletting, but cannot independently establish the Delhi rule.
uses.incremental_value: Helps delimit the persuasive reach of LAW:V21:GR:APPLICATION and prevents treating that application as a direct construction of the Delhi statute.
uses.limits: Andhra Pradesh rent legislation, quoted historically in a judgment; not Delhi law and not a complete statute history.

uses.issue: Whether a company amalgamation transferring tenancy and possession without written landlord consent can constitute a prohibited transfer in an analogous rent-control setting.
uses.law_quote: the tenant company has transferred all its interest in the tenanted premises in favour of the appellant No. 2
uses.reason: The Supreme Court application demonstrates that a court-sanctioned company amalgamation can effect transfer of tenancy and possession and that the absence of written landlord consent mattered under the Andhra Pradesh Act. The supplied target record, however, describes incorporation and operation of another company by the tenant firm's partners, not an amalgamation dissolving the tenant.
uses.standalone_value: Supports a corporate-transfer principle in its own amalgamation facts but does not establish that mere incorporation or shared directors equals transfer or parting with possession here.
uses.incremental_value: Can contextualize the petitioner's corporate-separation argument, while the factual difference between amalgamation and parallel operation materially limits the analogy.
uses.limits: Adopted application under the Andhra Pradesh Act and an amalgamation scheme; target record contains no comparable amalgamation finding.

uses.issue: Whether Delhi section 14(1)(b) reaches assignment or other modes of parting with possession, including involuntary transfers.
uses.law_quote: the amplitude of S. 14(b) of the Delhi Rent Control Act was wide enough not only to include any sublease but even an assignment or any other mode by which possession of the tenanted premises is parted
uses.reason: This Supreme Court unit expressly reports the reach of the Delhi provision and states that its amplitude includes assignment and other modes of parting with possession, even an involuntary sale. That bears directly on the petitioner's arguments concerning alleged testamentary or other transfer.
uses.standalone_value: Directly supports a broad reading of the disposition element of the Delhi ground, including transfers beyond conventional subleases.
uses.incremental_value: Adds authoritative interpretation to the statutory text, particularly against an argument that a transfer escapes section 14(1)(b) solely because it was involuntary or took a form other than a sublease.
uses.limits: This is General Radio's report of Parasaram, not the independently supplied full Parasaram opinion; the underlying facts involved liquidation sale.

uses.issue: Whether a Bombay protected-licensee/acquisition setting bears on the supplied Delhi subletting, assignment or possession question.
uses.law_quote: the licensee Esso Eastern Inc. had already acquired the status of deemed tenant under s. 15A of the Bombay Rent Act
uses.reason: No supplied target fact concerns a protected licence under Bombay section 15A, statutory acquisition of Esso, or the associated appointed-date regime. The current fixed Delhi ground does not require this unit to resolve any identified subquestion.
uses.standalone_value: Establishes the protected-licensee and acquisition context of Hindustan Petroleum only.
uses.incremental_value: Adds no identified assistance once the Delhi section 14(1)(b) materials are available because its protection turns on a different statute and factual mechanism.
uses.limits: Bombay Rent Act and specific acquisition context; no general Delhi eviction immunity is supplied.

uses.issue: Whether statutory vesting under the Esso acquisition regime supplies an exception or rule for the alleged private-company occupation in this case.
uses.law_quote: the Central Government became the lessee or tenant, as the case may be
uses.reason: The unit concerns tenancy vesting caused by a specific acquisition statute, notification and later statutory amalgamation. The allowed target record supplies no comparable statutory acquisition or vesting mechanism for Hitkari Brothers or M/s Anil & Co. Pvt. Ltd.
uses.standalone_value: Shows that a specific enactment could vest tenancy in government and successor entities in that statutory setting.
uses.incremental_value: No current incremental value because no supplied fact activates the Esso Acquisition Act or a comparable statutory vesting provision.
uses.limits: Specific Esso Acquisition Act/Bombay Rent Act regime; expressly not a general Delhi section 14(1)(b) rule.

uses.issue: Whether court-ordered amalgamation may avoid a written-consent objection and, conversely, whether the Delhi section 14(1)(b) issue remains available for later determination.
uses.law_quote: Prima facie, the rights of the transferor-company in the tenancy, contractual or statutory, are transferable on an amalgamation
uses.reason: The unit supplies a potentially contrary route: a prima facie view that amalgamation vesting might not require landlord consent and might lie outside section 14(1)(b). It simultaneously expressly reserves the actual eviction question and preserves the landlord's right to invoke the Rent Act. This matters as a limit on overgeneralizing corporate-transfer authorities, although the target record does not itself establish an amalgamation.
uses.standalone_value: Supports only a prima facie, reserved proposition concerning court-sanctioned amalgamation and confirms that any Delhi eviction consequence requires separate determination.
uses.incremental_value: Counters any categorical proposition that every corporate vesting automatically triggers section 14(1)(b), while remaining factually remote from mere incorporation by common partners.
uses.limits: Delhi High Court partial document; prima facie discussion only; the section 14(1)(b) eviction question was expressly reserved.

uses.issue: Whether the specific New Bank of India-to-Punjab National Bank statutory vesting scheme bears on this private tenancy dispute.
uses.law_quote: Where any. property is held by the transferor bank under any lease the transferee bank shall on and from the date of commencement of this scheme be deemed to have become the lessee
uses.reason: This unit creates lease succession for one named 1993 bank amalgamation. Neither named bank nor any analogous statutory scheme appears in the allowed record, so it cannot establish the status of M/s Anil & Co. Pvt. Ltd. or the respondent firm.

uses.issue: Whether the alleged subletting or transfer could be lawful based on its date and previous written landlord consent.
uses.law_quote: no tenant shall, without the previous consent in writing of the landlord
uses.reason: Section 16 directly supplements the fixed section 14(1)(b) question by specifying when subletting is deemed lawful and by requiring previous written consent for post-Act subletting or transfer/assignment. This bears on the respondent's assertion that the erstwhile landlord permitted family members or business under other names, while the supplied record does not itself state that such permission was written.
uses.standalone_value: Supplies statutory lawfulness and previous-written-consent requirements for subletting and transfer/assignment, but does not prove the existence, form or scope of consent in this case.
uses.incremental_value: Clarifies the consent issue beyond section 14(1)(b), especially the distinction between asserted permission and statutorily specified written consent.
uses.limits: Current reproduction is not an authenticated historical consolidation; exact commencement/date application must remain within the supplied text.

uses.issue: Whether notice provisions for a consensual or previously lawful sub-tenancy affect evaluation of the asserted consent defense.
uses.law_quote: with the previous consent in writing of the landlord
uses.reason: Section 17 assumes categories of sub-tenancies created with previous written consent or lawfully created before commencement and provides notice/dispute procedures. It helps contextualize what the Act contemplates as a recognized sub-tenancy, but the supplied target record contains no identified section 17 notice or section 17 Controller proceeding.
uses.standalone_value: Shows notice procedures associated with consensual or previously lawful sub-tenancies; it does not independently establish or defeat the section 14(1)(b) ground here.
uses.incremental_value: Provides context to sections 14(1)(b) and 16 if a claimed lawful sub-tenancy is asserted, while contributing little without evidence of statutory notice.
uses.limits: No section 17 notice or dispute procedure is identified in the allowed case segments; statutory reproduction is historically unverified.
